src: ; 14 triangle_raster — how a GPU draws a triangle: edge functions per pixel
; Every 3D image is made of triangles. Rasterization asks, for each pixel:
; is its center inside the triangle? GPUs answer with three EDGE FUNCTIONS
; (Pineda, 1988). For an edge V0 -> V1 and a pixel P:
;     E(P) = (V1y - V0y) * Px  -  (V1x - V0x) * Py  +  (V0y*(V1x - V0x) - V0x*(V1y - V0y))
; E >= 0 on the inner side of the edge. Inside the triangle all three are >= 0,
; and each E divided by the triangle's area is a BARYCENTRIC weight: how close
; P is to the opposite corner. Blending red, green and blue by those weights
; Coordinates are doubled (half-pixel units) so pixel centers 2x+1 are integers.
; The per-edge coefficients are computed by the assembler (.equ) and passed as
; kernel arguments, exactly like a driver sets up a real rasterizer.
;   __global__ void raster(uint32_t* fb, Edge e[3], int k, uint32_t bg) {
;       int w[3]; for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) w[i] = e[i].a * px + e[i].b * py + e[i].c;
; Watch for: no branches at all. Inside/outside is a predicate (@!P0 MOV),
; so every warp stays converged even along the triangle's edges.
; vertices in half-pixel units: A (top, red), B (bottom right, green), C (bottom left, blue)
; edge opposite A is C -> B, opposite B is A -> C, opposite C is B -> A
.equ AREA, EA_A * AX + EA_B * AY + EA_C      ; weight of A at A = twice the area
.equ KCOL, 255 * 65536 / AREA                ; weight -> 0..255 via one QMUL
LDC  R5, c[0]              ; --- edge opposite A: weight of red
MAD  R2, R5, R0, R6        ; wA = a*Px + b*Py + c
LDC  R5, c[3]              ; --- edge opposite B: weight of green
MAD  R3, R5, R0, R6        ; wB
LDC  R5, c[6]              ; --- edge opposite C: weight of blue
MAD  R4, R5, R0, R6        ; wC
MIN  R5, R2, R3            ; inside if min(wA, wB, wC) >= 0
LDC  R7, c[10]             ; 255 / area as Q16.16
QMUL R2, R2, R7            ; red   = wA * 255 / area
QMUL R3, R3, R7            ; green = wB * 255 / area
QMUL R4, R4, R7            ; blue  = wC * 255 / area
@!P0 MOV R2, R8                ; outside: background (predicated, no branch)
ADD  R9, R9, R10           ; pixel index y * 32 + x
